awd_titl_txt: I-Corps: Translation Potential of an Interface Designed for Real-time Monitoring of  Groundwater Levels and Assessment of Land Subsidence
awd_abstract_narration:
The broader impact of this I-Corps project is the development of a software solution that enhances the understanding of groundwater flow dynamics and land settlement. This software aligns with the sustainability goals mandated for local irrigation districts and groundwater sustainability agencies. By preventing the need for land repurposing, the software will safeguard the agricultural economy and preserve vital farmland. The solution will also improve scenario development tools used by engineering consulting companies, leading to more informed decision-making in groundwater sustainability planning. Additionally, the technology will assess future flood risk areas resulting from extensive groundwater extraction, providing valuable insights for insurers and reinsurers. This solution will help mitigate the negative impacts of groundwater drilling on critical civil infrastructure such as highways, bridges, and canals, potentially saving billions of dollars for counties and taxpayers.

This I-Corps project utilizes experiential learning coupled with a first-hand investigation of the industry ecosystem to assess the translation potential of the technology. This solution is based on the development of a product with a user-friendly interface designed for real-time monitoring of groundwater levels and the assessment of land subsidence caused by excessive groundwater withdrawal. The software integrates real-time observations from in-situ extensometers and remote airborne and satellite imaging. The technology employs a comprehensive workflow and methodology for reduced-order and machine learning-based surrogates. These surrogates are trained on data derived from physics-based, high-fidelity, numerical simulations. This approach enables accurate and efficient tracking of managed aquifer recharge and provides essential insights for groundwater sustainability and land subsidence prevention.

This award reflects NSF's statutory mission and has been deemed worthy of support through evaluation using the Foundation's intellectual merit and broader impacts review criteria.

por.por_cntn:
Modern society depends on a stable supply of critical minerals for clean energy technologies, infrastructure, and advanced manufacturing. At the same time, mining operations face increasing pressure to manage water resources responsibly and to ensure the long-term stability and safety of mine tailings facilities. The Hydro Nexus project addresses these challenges by developing a data-driven platform that improves how water resources are allocated and managed during mineral exploration, mineral processing, and mine tailings design.

 

Hydro Nexus brought together a multidisciplinary team that includes two doctoral researchers, a postdoctoral scholar from Stanford University, and an industry mentor with more than 35 years of experience in public utilities and venture capital. The core technology integrates satellite-based Interferometric Synthetic Aperture Radar (InSAR) data with proprietary data inversion methods, advanced data assimilation, machine learning, and artificial intelligence. This approach enables the extraction of actionable information about ground deformation, hydrology, and structural behavior that is difficult or costly to obtain using conventional methods.

 

The primary goal of the NSF I-Corps award was to validate and refine the project’s value propositions and customer segments, ensuring that the technology addresses real-world needs and can achieve product–market fit. During the life of the award, the team completed the National NSF I-Corps training program and conducted extensive customer discovery. In total, more than 200 interviews were carried out with stakeholders across the mining ecosystem, including junior and major mining companies, engineering firms, startups, and academic institutions.

 

A major outcome of this process was the identification of a strong product–market fit with mine tailings design teams, particularly Engineers of Record who are responsible for regulatory compliance and safety assurance. These professionals face significant challenges in integrating diverse data sources related to water resources, seepage, and geotechnical stability, and in producing defensible reports that meet regulatory and environmental standards. Customer discovery revealed that Hydro Nexus’s platform has the potential to reduce data processing and reporting timelines from several weeks to just days, while improving confidence in stability and safety assessments.

 

The intellectual merit of this project lies in advancing the application of satellite remote sensing, data inversion, and AI-driven analytics to complex hydrological and geotechnical problems. By combining these methods into a unified platform, the project demonstrates a novel way to monitor and evaluate mine tailings systems at scale.

 

The broader impacts are equally significant. Improved tailings stability assessments can reduce the risk of catastrophic failures, protect downstream communities and ecosystems, and support more responsible mineral production. More efficient water resource management also contributes to environmental sustainability in water-stressed regions.
